misconceptions: Mistaking satisfied neglect for simple rule-following

semantic_axes.description: Overconfidence about success versus willingness to follow authority

edges.boundary_rule: Complacent means confidence in existing success stops improvement or vigilance; compliant means obeying an instruction or rule, whether satisfied or not.
clues_a: past success treated as proof nothing can go wrong
clues_b: follows explicit instruction even when questioning it

misconceptions.M1: Mistaking satisfied neglect for simple rule-following
misconceptions.M3: Assuming good results remove the need for checking

chains.frame: Which word best describes Amina's approach to the situation?

beats.text: After one excellent mock exam, Amina stopped revising, certain she had already secured admission.
beats.decisive_clue: stopped studying because one success felt sufficient
beats.reason: The clue 'stopped studying because one success felt sufficient' points to satisfied inaction, not willing obedience.

beats.text: She still kept every revision notebook arranged neatly on her desk.
beats.decisive_clue: tidy notebooks do not mean she resumed preparing
beats.reason: The detail 'tidy notebooks do not mean she resumed preparing' leaves satisfied inaction as the better fit, not willing obedience.

chains.feedback_short: Tidy notebooks do not mean she resumed preparing; complacent still fits best.
chains.feedback_deep: complacent means so satisfied that needed improvement or vigilance stops; compliant means ready to follow rules or an authority. The first clue is "stopped studying because one success felt sufficient"; the next is "tidy notebooks do not mean she resumed preparing". Complacency rests on satisfaction; compliance rests on following a requirement.
chains.contrast_rule: Complacency rests on satisfaction; compliance rests on following a requirement.

hints.attention: Look at why the studying stopped.

hints.contrast: Complacency rests on satisfaction; compliance rests on following a requirement.
